cards.definitionChild: letting light through, so you can see what is on the other side
cards.sentence: The stream was so transparent we could count the pebbles.
cards.imagePrompt: Two children kneeling on a grassy bank, pointing at a shallow stream of clear water with every smooth pebble on its bed easy to see.
cards.why: Sense A is see-through, matching the key 'clear' on both LIVE items; no distractor (opaque, glass, window, thin, shiny, obvious) becomes right. Changed two fields. (1) The definition was a clause ('you can see straight through it'); it is now an adjective phrase in the style of the tier 3 exemplars. I took the reviewer's second option but said 'on the other side' rather than 'behind it', because in the card's own sentence the pebbles lie under the water, not behind it. It avoids 'glass' and 'window', both distractors on bank-vr-04-closest-meaning-35. (2) The image prompt showed a leaking sandwich, which makes no sense and reads as mess rather than see-through, and it was a different scene from the sentence. It now shows the sentence itself: children on the bank looking at pebbles through the water. Sentence, word class, tier 3 and one-sense are kept unchanged.
